title: Find The Evidence Across Both Units
objective: Finish a clear, evidence-based leadership-project review, then locate the evidence for all nine parts in two separate units and check the actual file total.

blocks.text: Today you will finish or clarify your own leadership-project review. This is Unit 2: Arts leadership, Part 2E: Leadership project review. A useful final review explains your role, what happened, what the evidence shows and what you would do next.
Then check the evidence across Unit 1: Arts practice and pathways and Unit 2: Arts leadership. Keep the units clearly separate, even when they sit in one digital folder.
Finding a file does not complete a missing experience. Keep gaps honest and ask for a workable next step. Your own review remains the main piece of work to improve today.

Staff · Silver Unit 2: Arts leadership; Part 2E: Leadership project review. This deck directly teaches completion and clarification of the pupil’s own 2E review. It also checks all nine parts, with listsPortfolio=true; checking a part does not teach or fabricate its missing activity. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Silver is the Level 2 Award in the Arts, qualification 500/9914/0. Keep Unit 1: Arts practice and pathways separately evidenced from Unit 2: Arts leadership. The Unit 1A arts challenge must not focus on leadership; the Unit 2 project cannot replace it. Mark P / A / N per part. One Attempted is allowed PER UNIT; any Not Attempted means Below Pass. Results are Pass / Below Pass. The whole Silver portfolio has a maximum of 20 files. Check the actual total, retaining separately locatable evidence for every part. Nine cumulative part files or two clearly sectioned unit files are possible layouts, not compulsory file quotas. Every locator names the actual file plus page, slide or timecode; “in arts log” is not sufficient. External evidence links must be public. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess. Delivery must be through a validated centre. Staff must confirm these conditions; the deck does not assert them as fulfilled. Moderators check the consistency of adviser marking; they do not reassess work. Advisers must not write pupil plans, reviews or evidence. Staff may prompt or accurately scribe the pupil’s exact words and confirmed selections, then check them back. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Silver while retaining the pupil’s full review, personal choices and actual evidence. No public showing, filming, personal disclosure or invented numerical quota is required. Missing Unit 1C audience experience/review/sharing and Unit 1D practitioner meeting/first-hand activity remain incomplete. Staff consult their serving decks and current EVENT_SLOT, PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT for arrangements; no new slot-dependent activity is claimed by this 2E deck. Fourteen 40-minute lessons support the programme, not the full 95 hours. Record actual additional activity toward the 60 guided and 35 independent hours.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Bring actual unit records and the pupil’s 2E draft. Readiness is determined by completed activity and evidence, not the position of this lesson in the timetable.

blocks.text: Return to the judgement you made
Open your project review and the real records it uses. Read or hear the conclusion you made about your leadership. Which sentence best shows what you learnt from a decision?
Put the supporting record beside that sentence. Check that the record shows your role, as well as the group’s finished artwork. Keep the real words from people in the team or taking part.
You need your two unit records, a pen and paper, or your usual accessible tool. You may speak, sign or dictate exact words for a scribe to check back with you.
If the project has not been delivered, keep your review labelled as preparation so far. Do not change the label just because this is the last planned lesson.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: The complete example conclusion, record and revision are on the page. Do not attribute them to pupils or treat agreement in the example as evidence of actual collaboration.

blocks.text: Check whether the conclusion reaches too far
Read this authored example conclusion: “The session finished, so our team worked well together.” Finishing tells us about the end of the session. It does not show how the team worked.
Here is an example record: “I asked which task needed help. We agreed to change the order, and I moved the paper to the next table.” The record gives a contribution that a review can discuss.
A more useful conclusion is: “I helped the team change the order after checking what was needed. Our agreement gave me a clear task.” This claim is linked to the example record.
Tell a listener what became clearer. These are teaching examples only. Your conclusion must grow from your own project and records.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Teach revision as evidence-based judgement. Do not make the review sound more successful on the pupil’s behalf. A retained judgement is acceptable when the existing evidence already supports it.

blocks.text: Make a reasoned change to your review
Use a simple sequence: read the claim, check the record, adjust the judgement, then explain the next step. The review should become more accurate, not merely longer.

In the example, the leader could add: “Next time I would check task order with the team before we start. That may reduce the need to move tools during the task.” This follows from the problem in the example.

blocks.title: Clarify the final leadership review
blocks.alt: Read a claim, check its evidence, adjust the judgement, and explain the next step.
blocks.caption: A clear review connects your conclusion to the project.

blocks.text: The leader cannot claim that the new order would always work. A next step is a plan with a reason until it has been tried. You can explain why it seems useful while naming that limit.
Read back a change before saving it. If a scribe helped, check every statement about what you thought or learnt. Keep your own view when someone offers a different interpretation.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Project the full card set or copy it onto paper. Keep the distinction between an arts-development challenge and a leadership project explicit without changing the pupil’s existing unit labels.

blocks.text: Match each record to the correct unit
Use two headings: Unit 1 — Arts practice and pathways; Unit 2 — Arts leadership. Match the four cards. Each is a labelled example of evidence, not a claim that you have completed it.

items: Card 1: A pupil’s action plan to develop their own drawing skill.
Card 2: A review of an arts event attended as an audience member, with evidence that the review was shared.
Card 3: A record of the pupil’s own leadership decisions while delivering the project.
Card 4: The pupil’s final review of their leadership project, using actual aims and feedback.

blocks.text: Check key: Unit 1 has 1 and 2. Unit 2 has 3 and 4. Card 1 belongs to the arts challenge. Leading a project cannot replace that personal arts-development work.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: All nine exact registered parts are printed here. This is a check of existing evidence; it does not declare these parts directly taught by the 2E deck or invent missing experiences.

blocks.text: Use the complete nine-part check
Keep each unit and part visible. Use these exact labels to find the work and check what the record needs to show.

items: 1A: Plan an arts challenge — your strengths, weaknesses and own action plan. The challenge must not focus on leadership.
1B: Implement and review the arts challenge — ongoing evidence, someone else’s review, and your own final review.
1C: Review arts events — an actual audience experience, your review of artistic qualities and creative impact, and evidence that you shared the review.
1D: Arts research — meet arts practitioners and gain first-hand workshop or event experience; research arts organisations, education and career pathways; summarise the influence in your own words.
2A: Plan the project and own leadership role.
2B: Plan practical issues — promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and a feedback plan.

blocks.title: Keep both units separately identifiable
blocks.alt: Unit 1 contains 1A to 1D. Unit 2 contains 2A to 2E. Every part needs a clear evidence location.
blocks.caption: Separate units; a clear location for every part.

blocks.text: A folder name cannot stand in for the activity itself. If a required experience or record is absent, keep the gap visible.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Support navigation without supplying the pupil’s judgement. Check actual files, including access to any public external evidence link. No mandatory filming or personal disclosure is needed.

blocks.text: Follow a locator all the way to the evidence
Choose one real review statement and its supporting record. Give a partner the actual file name plus page, slide or timecode. Ask them to open the place you named.

An example of the form is “Unit-2-review.pdf, page 4.” For sound or video, the file name and the start time of the relevant section help the reader find it. These example names must be replaced with your real ones.
The partner checks whether that place supports the statement. A clear file name is not enough if the page holds different work. Correct the location or narrow the claim yourself.
If the file will not open, record the access problem. Keep the original safe while you ask for help. Never invent a page or a clip to fill the space.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Give time to substantive 2E review before the file check. All routes retain full evidence expectations. Help combine files without losing process, others’ reviews or distinct unit/part records; do not require nine files or one per lesson.

blocks.text: Finish the review, then check the evidence set

Use the first part of this time to finish or clarify your own project review. Keep the aim, role, practical decisions, delivery, work with others and real feedback together. Explain achievements, limits, learning and a reasoned next step.

items: Core · Use accessible answers to complete the full review in your own words. Check any exact scribing. Link your judgement and next step to actual evidence, then locate all nine parts in their units and record gaps.
Extend · Complete the same full review and make each claim fit the record. Check the nine parts, exact locators and actual file total, keeping the two units clear.

Challenge · Complete the same full review and explain a limit or differing view in the evidence. Check all nine parts and test whether another reader can follow your evidence locations without guessing.

blocks.text: Count the actual files in the whole Silver evidence set. Record “My total is __ files; the cap is 20.” Nine part files are one possible layout, not a rule. Two unit files with clear part sections can also work.
If you exceed the cap, ask for help to combine records safely. Recheck every locator after a change and keep the source work safe until the new files are checked.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: Use the actual portfolio count and evidence status. Do not infer completion or a result from a neat folder, a ticked checklist or the end of the sequence.

blocks.text: State what is clear and what still needs action
Tell a listener one conclusion from your final review and the evidence behind it. Explain the next step you chose. The listener can check your meaning, but the judgement remains yours.

Give your actual file total and show where the two units sit. Name any gap and the action needed. A missing practitioner meeting, audience experience, review or sharing step needs real completion, not a new label.
Save your final review with its locator. Keep the gap note alongside the relevant part. Staff will assess the work against Silver requirements; this file check does not promise an award result.

print.intro: Complete your own Unit 2, Part 2E leadership-project review using real evidence. Then check all nine parts across the two units, accurate evidence locations and the actual file total against the twenty-file cap.
focusRows: My full review: aim, role, decisions, delivery, work with others, real feedback, achievements, limits, learning and a reasoned next step
Unit 1: Arts practice and pathways. 1A: Plan an arts challenge. 1B: Implement and review the arts challenge. 1C: Review arts events. 1D: Arts research.

Unit 2: Arts leadership. 2A: Plan the project and own leadership role. 2B: Plan practical issues. 2C: Effective arts leadership in delivery. 2D: Working effectively with others. 2E: Leadership project review.
Each item’s actual filename plus page, slide or timecode; my actual file total against the cap of 20; gaps and next actions
tiers: Core · Complete the full review through accessible answers in your own words. Check exact scribing, link judgement and next step to evidence, and locate all nine parts with honest gaps.
Extend · Complete the same full review and clarify unsupported claims. Check all nine parts, two separate units, exact locators and actual file total.
Challenge · Complete the same full review and weigh an evidence limit or differing view. Check all nine parts and test whether another reader can follow each locator.
checks: The pupil completed or clarified a substantive review of their actual leadership project, with gaps honestly labelled.
Judgements, achievements, limits, learning and a reasoned next step are the pupil’s own and linked to evidence.
Unit 1: Arts practice and pathways and Unit 2: Arts leadership remain separately identifiable, with all nine parts checked.
Each required item has an actual file name plus page, slide or timecode; missing activities remain incomplete.
The actual total was counted against the whole-Silver cap of 20 files; no nine-file or per-lesson quota was imposed.
